title: Bramble Analytics post-incident debrief & mitigations sync
summary: Debrief of the 2026-10-03 production degradation where long-tail token latency spiked causing customer-facing timeouts. Discussed root causes (autoscaler instability + cold KV cache + fallback routing misconfig), short-term mitigations (increase autoscale headroom, pin fallback model, extend prefix cache TTL), and mid-term reliability work (improved rollout canary, better tracing for KV cache evictions, runbench for 90th/99th p99 tail). Agreed on action owners and follow ups: Redwood to provide incident timeline and mitigations doc, Bramble to run a guided load test with traffic shape, both to schedule a joint private deployment benchmark for dedicated capacity if needed.
topics: Fallback routing and model variant compatibility
next_steps: Redwood to send incident timeline + raw metric snapshots (by 2026-10-08)
Bramble to run a 2-hour guided load test with the Redwood SE (proposed 2026-10-12)
Set up dedicated canary with extended cache TTL and pinned fallback model for 1 week (start target 2026-10-15)
Share security whitepaper and KMS integration notes (Redwood)
Schedule a private benchmarking session for dedicated capacity if tests show tail latency improvement
action_items: Lena Park: compile incident timeline with correlation graphs and upload to shared drive (due 2026-10-08)
Marco Ruiz: prepare runbook patch to change autoscaler headroom and fallback routing flag; include rollback steps (due 2026-10-09)
Omar Jackson: provision test dataset and traffic shape for guided load test, include 95/99 percentile goals (due 2026-10-11)
Dana Lee: confirm KMS and audit log requirements and send checklist (due 2026-10-10)
Victor Huang: provide sample traces for a typical slow request path to help reproduce cache eviction scenario (due 2026-10-09)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Bramble Head of Platform), Omar Jackson (SRE), Dana Lee (Security), Victor Huang (Data Eng)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about 45 minutes to an hour. Main goal is to debrief the customer-impacting latency spike last Friday and agree mitigations. Marco, do you want to start with the symptom summary?

[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Sure, I can. So the core symptom was a long tail token latency increase starting ~09:12 UTC on 2026-10-03. P50 looked fine but p95/p99 shot up, and several requests hit the 6 second api timeout and retried which amplified load. There was a cascade: autoscaler trimmed pods during a scale event, then KV cache warmed slowly, and fallback routing pushed some traffic to a larger variant but our compatibility check failed for a small percent, which hit a slow path.

[00:50] Priya Menon: Quick clarifying Q, when you say "compatibility check" do you mean the model variant mapping? We saw a lot of 503s and then higher latency; our app's retry logic interpreted that as transient and retried aggressively.

[01:05] Marco Ruiz: Yeah, so we have a routing policy that falls back to a quantized variant in a different region when local capacity is low. In this event the fallback model had a slightly different tokenizer mapping in the converted artifact, leading to a slower decode path for some requests. Also worth noting our autoscaler threshold was at 60% CPU which allowed a brief trough where headroom was insufficient during the traffic burst.

[01:32] Omar Jackson: Sorry to interrupt, but the logs we collected showed a spike in cache misses for prefix cache around the same time. It looked like there was an eviction wave. Could that be due to memory pressure because nodes were being cycled?

[01:46] Marco Ruiz: That's likely. We saw node replacements in the cloud provider metrics coincident with a rolling update. The combination of rolling updates plus aggressive pod reallocation is a risky window.

[02:05] Dana Lee: From security side, customers are asking how this impacts audit logs and KMS operations. There was a question whether any keys rotated during the incident which could cause additional latency.

[02:20] Lena Park: Good point. To be explicit, there was no customer KMS rotation triggered by Redwood during that window; keys were stable. But we'll include the exact KMS logs in the timeline export.

[02:36] Victor Huang: I want to call out that our traffic pattern includes many short chat-like sessions with prefix reuse. When prefix cache misses, tail latency goes up more than for single-shot completions because the KV cache rebuild is heavier.

[02:55] Marco Ruiz: Exactly, so recommended short-term mitigations: increase autoscaler headroom to 30% extra capacity during peak windows, extend prefix cache TTL to avoid evictions during rolling updates, and pin fallback model variant only after a compatibility check pass.

[03:18] Priya Menon: Operationally, how quickly can you change the autoscaler policy? We can't afford a prolonged risk window in production.

[03:28] Marco Ruiz: We can push a config change to the scaling policy within 24 hours, and it has a simple rollback. We'll provide the patch and the runbook.

[03:40] Omar Jackson: Will that increase cost? Bramble needs to sign off on spending if it permanently increases reserved capacity.

[03:48] Lena Park: For the short term, it's a temporary headroom bump — cost is marginal for the test period. If you need a long-term solution, we can propose a Dedicated pool with pinned capacity and stronger SLOs. That's where the committed pricing kicks in.

[04:05] Priya Menon: Ok. We are open to a temporary bump but we'll want data before considering Dedicated. Can Redwood share a p99 cost estimate versus hosted during the canary?

[04:18] Marco Ruiz: Yes, I'll produce a per-token cost delta for the canary and for a projected dedicated pool.

[04:30] Dana Lee: On compliance: we need to validate that the audit logs cover the fallback routing decision and the model variant id. Also need assurance that the private key access logs show no anomalies.

[04:44] Lena Park: We'll include audit log extracts and the model catalog mapping table. We'll redact any PII.

[04:54] Victor Huang: For reproduction, we can give you a sample traffic replay that reproduces the tail latency after warming a few prefixes, we'll also attach a capture from our edge proxies.

[05:06] Marco Ruiz: That will be really helpful. Also a note: your retry policy triggered by 502/503 is amplifying load. One mitigation is to return a 429-like signal earlier so clients don't retry immediately.

[05:22] Priya Menon: Hm, we prefer not to change client logic during peak launches. Any server-side debounce options?

[05:30] Marco Ruiz: We can enable an early-throttle policy at the edge to convert certain queueing thresholds into 429s. That avoids a client push. It's a config flip with immediate effect.

[05:42] Omar Jackson: Regarding observability, can we get more fine-grained traces for KV cache evictions? Right now our traces only show request-level spans not the backend cache internal timing.

[05:56] Marco Ruiz: We can ship an instrumented build that emits eviction spans and size histograms. It'll add some overhead but should be low. We can enable it for the canary only.

[06:12] Priya Menon: Sounds good. Let's talk about rollout safety — you mentioned a canary plan?

[06:20] Marco Ruiz: Proposed canary: 5% of traffic to be routed to a config with extended cache TTL + pinned fallback model + early-throttle enabled. Monitor p95/p99 and error rate for 24 hours, then 25% for 24 hours, rollback if p99 increases > 20% from baseline. We'll also enable the new tracing only in the canary.

[06:45] Victor Huang: If we see regression in the canary, what's the rollback path?

[06:52] Lena Park: Immediate config flip to previous policy, and we'll disable the tracing if it impacts performance. Marco will own rollback and provide a play-by-play to your SRE channel.

[07:05] Dana Lee: One more compliance question: for a dedicated pool, can we ensure VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?

[07:13] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering/PrivateLink. There are onboarding steps and a short compliance review. We'll send the Private deployment checklist.

[07:28] Priya Menon: Timeline wise, we want the guided load test next week and the brief config change applied as soon as possible.

[07:36] Lena Park: Action items we'll capture and share. Any other open Qs?

[07:42] Omar Jackson: One small note — our proxy team observed a flurry of connections from a single IP block during the incident which coincided with retries. Could be legitimate but we want you to help confirm it's not a bot amplification pattern.

[07:56] Marco Ruiz: We'll correlate the request ids you provide with Redwood ingress logs.

[08:04] Priya Menon: OK, that's it from me. Thanks everyone.

[08:10] Lena Park: Recap: Redwood sends incident timeline + metrics, Marco provides runbook patch and tracing build, Bramble runs guided load test and shares traces, Dana confirms KMS checklist. We'll reconvene after the guided test to decide if a dedicated canary is appropriate. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
